TGTrack: Temporal Generative Learning for Unified Single Object Tracking
Wanting Geng1, Xin Chen2,∗, Chuanyu Sun1, Jie Zhao1, Ben Kang1, Dong Wang1, Huchuan Lu1
1Dalian University of Technology
2City University of Hong Kong
Abstract
Existing single object trackers typically treat temporal
modeling superficially by passing limited inter-frame in-
formation, such as propagated tokens or template updates,
without intrinsic temporal supervision learning. To address
this limitation, we propose TGTrack, a new unified tracking
framework that incorporates a temporally generative super-
vision task to guide the model in learning temporal dynam-
ics. The core of TGTrack is a temporally generative learn-
ing paradigm equipped with a transformer-based genera-
tive decoder, which consists of a gated fusion module and
an autoregressive prediction mechanism. This joint design
enables the model to infer future scenarios from preceding
information, thereby improving its ability to model both vi-
sual appearance and temporal dynamics. Furthermore, we
introduce a time token embedding to explicitly encode the
temporal position of each frame. Experiments on 11 bench-
marks spanning five modalities show that TGTrack achieves
state-of-the-art performance in robust unified tracking. For
instance, TGTrack-B384 achieves an AUC of 75.3% on La-
SOT. Code is available at https://github.com/wtg1/TGTrack.
1. Introduction
Single object tracking (SOT) is a fundamental task in com-
puter vision, which aims to continuously locate a specific
target throughout a video sequence given its initial bound-
ing box. With the rapid advancement of deep neural net-
works and large-scale training, recent RGB-based track-
ers [1, 8, 36, 68, 69] have achieved remarkable perfor-
mance. To handle more challenging scenarios such as low
illumination, severe occlusion, or fast motion, researchers
have extended SOT to multi-modal tracking by incorporat-
ing complementary modalities such as depth [61], thermal
infrared [26, 27], event streams [52], and natural language
descriptions [31, 51]. Building upon these advances, recent
works [11, 20, 21, 54, 72] have aimed to develop unified

However, both RGB-based and unified trackers generally
tend to overemphasize architectural design and modality fu-
sion, while overlooking the importance of temporal model-
ing, which limits their adaptability to dynamic target ap-
pearance changes. To address this issue, recent works have
explored temporal modeling strategies that can be broadly
categorized into two paradigms. The first paradigm, shown
in Fig.1(a), updates template frames with handcrafted pa-
rameters [9, 11, 23, 59], making the model sensitive to pa-
rameter settings and limiting its generalization. The second
paradigm, shown in Fig.1(b), propagates a small number of
temporal context tokens across frames [1, 22, 28, 57, 68, 70]
to capture temporal dynamics. Despite these advances, both
paradigms still encode temporal information implicitly by
injecting temporally relevant contents into the input but lack
explicit supervision, hindering their ability to model tempo-
ral dependencies and appearance transitions.

aware learning objective that explicitly guides the model to
